# Bounded actual-consumer validation

Prepared, not executed. Root reviews the seven production files and independent
tests before running this wrapper. Its parent is the unchanged, explicitly
hashed authored validation driver. It never executes commands from stored
results or selection metadata. The wrapper adds actual finite operation/Meaning
and selected opaque-Basis tests to the eleven existing declaration/type/effect/
source/CLI targets. Source inputs are recorded before and after every stage;
the declared map remains an incomplete build/runtime/fixture closure.

Use the actual Homebrew Rust1.98.1 latest mode, then capture the fixed forty
before/after comparisons without another Cargo command, then run Rust1.85.0
MSRV. Both modes share the existing target, jobs2, incremental0 and debug0.
Root coordinates all consumers of that target; the inherited advisory lock
covers only these validation-driver invocations. No new target is allocated.

Keep all actual failures and attempt directories. Version, formatting,
all-target compilation, four existing shared-type unit tests, actual integration
tests, denied-warning Clippy and CLI rebuild are separate stages. Expected
selection is not a result. Three existing sized tests remain ignored; two
unrelated3000-file import stress cases and the4000-source differential suite
remain explicitly excluded. No new maximum quantum case is generated.

The parent writes actual stdout/stderr directly to retained files and enforces
a1200-second child timeout. This bounds each direct subprocess only; it is not
a process-group or external-progeny cleanup guarantee and provides no global
disk quota. Existing small tests and root coordination constrain this run.

No Lean build/audit/replay, general source/family preservation, native rule,
guarantee admission, common-checker completion, canonical std API or same-commit
release readiness follows from these bounded checks. Both QLV1 scoped guarantees
and broader pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT duties retain their exact limits.
